limits: Author inspection of the complete visible tasks and accepted forms, not a new linguistic review or native certification.
Editorial grammar-study estimates, not an official item syllabus, complete JLPT curriculum, vocabulary level or proficiency assessment.

All primary anchors come from the inspected Bunpro index; the secondaryChecks list identifies the exact secondary entries compared, not a claim that every primary anchor has an exact secondary counterpart.
Extended tsumori predicates and established koto ni shite iru practices use documented semantic-family mappings rather than separately indexed labels for every ending.
Article counts describe linked practice, not the reading difficulty of every passage or articles without exercises.

policy.disagreements: Use the applicable primary entry and record differing secondary placements; do not average or silently choose the harder source.
policy.missingExactPrimarySense: Use an explicitly identified exact secondary construction when established; otherwise omit jlpt and record the unresolved scope.
policy.taskBoundary: Grade required grammar and substantive contrast, including the base fixed-choice task, not only the easiest key or hardest string anywhere in the object.
policy.preservation: Keep natural examples, translations, answers, stable identities, introduction groups, recommendations and lexical help unchanged.

officialCaveat.inspectedSection: Why Test Content Specifications are no longer available after the 2010 revision.
officialCaveat.conclusion: Official competence descriptions and samples do not provide an exhaustive current grammar-item list.

Unchanged state, not occasional adverb mama or the separate N2 mama ni construction.

senseExceptions.reason: Primary N5 dake covers exclusive only/just; primary N2 dake wa adds a different particle. Neither is silently treated as an exact level for bare maximum extent.

senseExceptions.scope: Approximate duration in the sole base choice for kiri-estimate-bus-wait.
senseExceptions.reason: Primary concentration bakari and recent-completion ta bakari do not establish this distinct quantity sense. Optional approximation answers elsewhere do not increase those levels.

primaryScopeNotes.note: Main lessons separate future intention from intended-role/pretending/belief uses. Extending the latter family to predicative self-view and completion-belief endings is an editorial mapping, not a separately published exact-pattern level. Do not import the suggestion that every belief is false.
The main lesson explicitly says wa is often omitted: ori ni is within the ori ni wa entry's scope.

Keep broad-period koro separate from vocabulary-card levels, and retain the primary's noun-interval/ongoing-verb-interval split. These family mappings are task estimates, not claims of a sharp cognitive boundary.

Both primary entries overlap. The main N4 entry directly supports noun dake de naku, noun mo; use N4 for those simple tasks. Level provenance does not endorse all ancillary restrictions in the lesson.
Established koto ni shite iru practices are mapped to the N3 chosen-action family. Optional practice alternatives do not increase the N4 you ni suru base-choice tasks.
Inspected the main About section. A forum response returned by simplified extraction is not treated as the main lesson or a published level for maximum extent.

decisions.rationale: The choice distinguishes factual nominalization from an explanatory wake conclusion.
The complete koto ni natte iru rule construction is required, not merely the noun koto.
Distinguish impossibility from the experience/occurrence reading of koto ga nai.
Preserve the reviewed pilot's N3 classification: the hazu/beki contrast, not the easier answer alone.
Preserve the reviewed N4 before/after contrast, including relative-time attachment.
Preserve the reviewed N4 distinction between about to act, acting, and just finished.
Choose the nominalizer required by the complete predicate/perception construction.
Distinguish an unnecessary action from a circumstance-based constraint.
Recognize wake ni wa ikanai rather than denying an inference.
The negative action before wake ni wa ikanai creates the separately listed cannot-not construction.
Distinguish impossibility, a practical constraint, and rejection of a necessary inference.
The visible choice contrasts ability with an actual past experience; unusual scenario vocabulary is not graded.
Nonpast koto ga aru means occasional occurrence, not past experience.
Distinguish an explicitly personal decision from an arrangement or resulting calculation.
The verb's relative time selects a purpose or an actual cause before the printed tame ni.
The task distinguishes a causal tame relation from a compensating kawari relation, or selects completed-event tame.
The literal okage/sei contrast is required; no general vocabulary levels are consulted.
Distinguish substitution from using an existing occasion for an additional action.
The hou/hoka contrast includes the N4 hoka ni addition construction.
Only the requested ta/nai attachment before printed hou ga ii is tested; contextual vocabulary is supported.
The task requires kagiri's evidence scope or maintained/unless condition, including its contrast with baai.
Compare an expected standard with a construction that conventionally marks reproach.
Distinguish an eventual process outcome (sue/ageku) from an independent added fact (ue ni).
These explicitly request only the noun/na-adjective modifier before printed baai; optional de aru is not required.
These controlled tasks require conditional formation, polarity or relative event timing, not vocabulary levels.
The tested conditional families and prospective/completed baai attachment are N4 anchors; incidental vocabulary is excluded.
Includes the endpoint answer whose actual choices explicitly contrast made with made ni, not just the two deadline answers.
Basic noun predicates, phrase scope, case roles, retained topic/inclusion and particle pronunciation; glossed label vocabulary does not set the level.
Basic wa/ga/mo interpretation and case-preserving combinations. Interpretation labels are glossed and are not vocabulary prerequisites.
The noun phrase no koto is already supplied; only its direct-object particle is elicited.
Only a noun's no, a na-adjective's na, or the supplied verb's plain modifier is elicited before printed baai/tame.
Produce the explicitly requested koto nominalization; the outer ni tsuite relation is already printed and not contrasted.
Topic, directed target, standpoint, purpose and layered noun/fact interpretation require the corresponding compound relations, not merely an easy answer label.
The N no tsumori intended-role reading is contrasted with inference, not merely V-ru future intention. Map its semantic family to Bunpro's N2 tsumori de lesson.
The verb-based options contrast norms with predictions or plans; optional alternative normative formulations do not increase the level.
Affirm or deny a future-action intention, including ordinary past inflection of that intention. No completed-action belief is elicited.
Positive/negative future intention, not the separate completed-action belief sense.
The V-ru/V-ta contrast changes intention into a belief about completion. The extended belief family maps to N2 tsumori de, not the N5 future-plan entry.
Contrast current self-assessment with a plan to become something. N2 is an editorial semantic-family mapping from tsumori de, not a claim that the source separately lists every predicate ending.
All tasks explicitly contrast a completed-action belief with an earlier intention and a current inference; apply the extended tsumori semantic-family mapping.
Ordinary hazu attachment and tense locate an expectation or inference; actual fulfillment is not an extra grammar level.
The V-ru/V-ta mono contrast is general tendency versus recurring past recollection.
The task contrasts a personal mono/mon justification with a wake conclusion.
Every fixed-choice task includes the substantive mama retained-state contrast; optional formal copulas do not add a higher level.
The fixed choices explicitly require distinguishing the hoka nai no-alternative construction from the other stances, even when hoka nai is not the key.
The actual choices use N3 shika nai, not N2 hoka nai. More advanced optional typed alternatives do not raise the label.
The fixed choices explicitly require distinguishing the hoka nai no-alternative construction from the other stances, even when hoka nai is not the key.
The actual choices use N3 shika nai, not N2 hoka nai. More advanced optional typed alternatives do not raise the label.
The fixed choices include koto ni shite iru as an established chosen practice. This is the aspectual member of the N3 koto ni suru family.
The actual choices use N4 you ni naru/you ni suru and inference. Optional koto ni shite iru does not raise these tasks.
The targeted contrast is following a model versus acting under guidance/conditions.
The blank is one particle, but its job is distinguishing the full ue ni/ue de constructions.
Unchanged mama state and transition with naru are the explicit semantic contrast.
Ta/nai attachment is interpreted within the unchanged-state mama construction.
Distinguish adverbial you ni from noun-modifying you na within a comparison or example.
Choose the potential polarity of an enabled/prevented outcome before purpose you ni.
The task interprets new ability versus habit, or the polarity of a deliberately maintained practice.
The actual outside/inside alternatives include the separately listed no uchi group-membership construction.
The fixed alternatives use hoka/naka; optional uchi wording does not increase the level.
Distinguish the hoka nai construction in the fixed choices from no need.
The remaining redo-file pair uses shika nai versus koto wa nai; optional hoka nai does not raise it.
Interpret the time window or change occurring within it, including negative uchi ni.
Bunpro separately places noun no aida ni at N3; apply that noun-interval family to its wa/ni contrast.
The remaining interval tasks use Bunpro's separately listed N4 te iru aida family.
Toki versus koro as reference time versus a broad period; the primary koro entry explicitly covers broad spans, not only clock suffixes.
Ori occurs in the actual fixed choices, not just optional accepted answers. Bunpro's ori ni wa lesson explicitly also covers ori ni without wa.
Sai occurs in the fixed choices; optional ori does not raise the label to N1.
The remaining recurrence task contrasts tabi with toki, without requiring the optional formal occasion markers.
The fixed choices include kagiri's limit-of-possibility construction, contrasted with a desired amount.
No exact Bunpro bare extent-dake lesson was established: N5 exclusive dake and N2 dake wa are different scopes. Use the secondary's explicit N3 extent entry, not a fabricated primary assignment.
Polarity is determined by stated degree versus the hodo-negative comparison construction.
Both sides explicitly contrast the N3 proportional ba-hodo construction with wanted extent; the secondary extent-dake entry also agrees at N3.
The complete contrast is degree/minimum kurai or hodo versus concessive noni; do not label the easier noni answers in isolation.
This fixed-choice key is approximate quantity bakari, not concentration bakari. Use the secondary's exact N2 approximation entry; primary N3 concentration is not evidence for this sense.
Required kiri, approximation and last-event/tabi contrasts. Optional nomi/kagiri or approximate bakari answers do not raise the remaining questions.
The fixed choices contrast hodo approximation with exclusive dake.
The remaining quantity choices use basic kurai/gurai and exclusive dake; optional hodo/bakari do not raise them.
The te/ta contrast distinguishes concentration bakari from recent-completion bakari.
Toka is the sole correct base choice, not merely an optional alternative to a basic noun connector.
Example marking, suggestion demo, shi addition/reasons and the shi/noni interpretation contrast.

The remaining tasks elicit basic noun joining, tari examples/variation/denial, te/de connections, both-inclusion or alternatives. Optional more advanced connectors/formal copulas do not increase the level.
All six interpretation tasks explicitly distinguish concessive noni from resource/time/tool noni.
Wari ni/kuse ni is the sole correct base choice in these tasks, unlike advanced optional alternatives in the other overlap questions.
The required base tasks are noni versus node, or ordinary noni attachment. Optional kuse/wari alternatives and background phrases do not increase the level.
Named dake formation/scope and ordinary mo addition; distractors do not turn a specified formation task into a requirement to master every focus particle.
The learner is explicitly asked to form only the dake pattern; this differs from the open dake/shika polarity task.
Interpret or form the complete shika-negative restriction, including choosing dake versus shika from the complete sentence.
Determine the affirmative implication of shika with a negative predicate, or choose the restriction particle from the printed polarity.
The simple noun-plus-dake-de-naku pattern fits Bunpro's N4 entry. Its overlapping N3 expansion is recorded as an overlap, not automatically selected.
Sae is required by the actual choices or quotation. Optional sura variants do not turn these into N1 tasks.
The noun-based demo inclusion/suggestion construction, not connective demo.
Number plus mo: an unexpectedly large quantity or not even one. These are distinct from ordinary additive mo.
Form emphatic made or explicitly distinguish emphatic inclusion from its endpoint meaning.
Interpret sae plus a conditional as sufficient here, rather than as exclusivity or an event that already happened.
